subject: platform/aws
auditor: agent session (Claude), quality round 108, see run record
professional: a senior AWS cloud/security engineer who reviews multi-account landing zones; they check first that GitHub OIDC trust is pinned by exact aud+sub so fork PRs and other branches cannot assume roles, that PR-reachable roles cannot read data, that permissions boundaries cannot be escaped, that state buckets are private/encrypted/versioned per account, that spend guards exist, and that the README matches the policies

evidence.correctness: OIDC trust recomputed with exact-match StringEquals semantics (IAM condition operators; independent evaluator in the auditor's scratchpad, evalpol.py, which parses bootstrap/bootstrap.yaml itself): github-plan accepts only repo:Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo:pull_request with aud sts.amazonaws.com, rejects another repo's PR, a workflow_dispatch token and an aws-prod environment token; github-apply accepts only :environment:aws-prod. The bootstrap plan role's deny-data-reads works as claimed (s3:GetObject outside state, kms:Decrypt outside the state key and GetSecretValue all explicitDeny). But the per-stack gha-<repo>-<stack>-plan roles in the workload accounts (stacks/github-oidc/account-roles/main.tf:213-234) evaluate to allow for s3:GetObject on another stack's state in the same bucket (plus kms:Decrypt on the shared state key), on any object in the account, dynamodb:Scan and sqs:ReceiveMessage, contradicting their own comment (main.tf:9-10, 43) and the deny list the member-account github-plan-readonly role carries (modules/account-baseline/main.tf:85-110). The workload permissions boundary (main.tf:135-167) does not require child roles to carry it, so a bounded role with IAM rights can mint an unbounded one. ReadOnlyAccess's action families were taken from memory (docs.aws.amazon.com unreachable: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so correctness is 2 with these as the reason, not the cap.
evidence.completeness: Checked against README 'Layout', 'Apply order' and 'The bootstrap': bootstrap creates the OIDC provider, KMS key, state bucket and both roles (works as written); configure.sh creates aws-prod/aws-llm with a custom 'main' branch policy and sets the two variables (matches GitHub REST shape); spend stack has per-account budgets 50/80/forecast, freeze SCP action, anomaly monitor, kill switch (dry run by default); github-oidc and findings are not in priv-aws-apply.yml (README admits it); the workload plan roles are not used by any workflow yet (only a template in stacks/saas-starter/ci/saas-starter.yml); priv-aws-plan.yml offers workflow_dispatch (line 22, allowed at 114) but a dispatch token's sub is ref:refs/heads/<branch>, which github-plan never trusts, so that path cannot plan; the LLM red-team job (priv-security-gate.yml:162-164) expects an AWS role trusting environment:paid-agents that no file under platform/aws defines (vars.ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_AWS_ROLE_ARN). Nothing is applied yet (AWS_ACCOUNT_ID unset), so end-to-end could not be run.

evidence.fitness: Job walked: the owner runs the CloudFormation bootstrap from CloudShell and configure.sh, then merges apply the management stacks. That path is coherent and a senior engineer would sign off on the management-account part. They would not sign off on putting customer data in the apps account while any same-repo PR can assume a workload plan role that reads S3 objects, DynamoDB items and SQS messages and print them into a public Actions log.
evidence.domain: Compared with AWS's multi-account / Security Reference Architecture practice: Organization with OUs, SCPs (no leaving, no disabling detective controls, region deny, no root, no users/keys), RCP data perimeter, org CloudTrail to object-locked log archive, GuardDuty/Security Hub/Config delegated admin, per-account state buckets, OIDC with exact aud+sub, no long-lived keys except a rotated transitional user, budgets + budget actions + anomaly detection. Departures: the permissions boundary lacks the standard 'iam:CreateRole/PutRolePermissionsBoundary only with this boundary' self-enforcement; PR-reachable roles in workload accounts get ReadOnlyAccess without data denies; apply trust keys only on the environment name, not the workflow (job_workflow_ref).

defects.what: Workload-account plan roles (gha-<repo>-<stack>-plan), assumable by any same-repository pull_request, have ReadOnlyAccess with only PutObject/DeleteObject/GetSecretValue/SSM denied: they can read every S3 object (including other stacks' state, decryptable with the shared state key), DynamoDB items, SQS messages and Lambda environment in shared-infra, apps and security, and a PR could print them into a public Actions log. The member-account github-plan-readonly and the bootstrap github-plan carry a full deny-data-reads list; this role does not, and its comments claim the opposite.

The workload permissions boundary does not enforce itself on roles that bounded roles create (no Deny on iam:CreateRole / iam:PutRolePermissionsBoundary unless iam:PermissionsBoundary is the workload boundary). The apply role may attach any managed policy (e.g. AdministratorAccess) to its <stack>-* roles, so a bounded role with IAM rights can create an unbounded role and then rewrite the gha-* roles' trust.
Plan-role comments claim prefix-scoped state reads and no secret/data reads; ReadOnlyAccess makes both false (see the high defect).
No test asserts the OIDC aud condition or the plan roles' deny statements; bootstrap.yaml has no test at all beyond linters, so seeded changes to its trust or the gha plan deny survive.

github-apply trust keys only on the environment name; any workflow on main that declares environment aws-prod (including a pull_request_target job, whose ref is main and so passes the branch policy) gets AdministratorAccess in the management account. A customised sub claim with job_workflow_ref pinned to priv-aws-apply.yml would close it.

priv-aws-plan.yml offers workflow_dispatch and lets the plan job run on it, but a dispatch token's subject (ref:refs/heads/<branch>) never matches github-plan's :pull_request trust, so a manual plan always fails at assume-role.

README 'Checks' says six stacks, 9 tofu test runs, 15 pytest tests; there are 17 stacks and 35 pytest tests. Layout omits dns, site, edge-api, saas-starter, email-ops and four product stacks; Apply order names `edge` and `products`, which are not directories.
The apply role's KeepTheStateKey denies do not cover kms:UpdateAlias/DeleteAlias on alias/tofu-state, which both workflows resolve to pick the backend key.

priv-security-gate.yml's adversarial-llm job expects an AWS role trusting environment:paid-agents (vars.ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_AWS_ROLE_ARN); no file under platform/aws defines it (github-llm-gate trusts main and aws-llm only), against 'everything as code'.

verdict: Below the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2) and not finished (completeness 2). The management-account bootstrap is senior-grade: exact aud+sub OIDC trust that fork PRs cannot reach, a plan role whose data denies hold under IAM evaluation, a hardened state bucket, and spend guards with honest limits. The workload-account roles in stacks/github-oidc are not: their PR-reachable plan roles omit the data-read denies every other plan role here carries (account-roles/main.tf:219), the permissions boundary is escapable by roles it bounds, and no test would catch either. Smallest safe fix: give gha-*-plan the same deny-data-reads list as modules/account-baseline (S3 GetObject outside the state bucket, DynamoDB, SQS, logs, Lambda GetFunction) plus a tftest assertion; add a boundary self-enforcement Deny. IaC tests (tofu test, checkov, cfn-lint) could not be run in this session; the README's results line is stale.
